record.paper_title: Hénon maps: a list of open problems
record.original_question: For a holomorphic automorphism of a compact Kähler surface with positive entropy, is Condition 3′ equivalent to Conditions 1 and 2, and do the quasi-hyperbolic analogues of Questions 20, 21, and 22 hold for such surface automorphisms?

evidence.quote: Question 25. — Is Condition 3′ equivalent to 1 and 2? And do Questions 20, 21, 22 above hold for quasi-hyperbolic surface automorphisms?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a compact Kähler surface and $f:X\to X$ a holomorphic automorphism with positive topological entropy. Let $\mathcal{S}$ denote the set of saddle periodic points of $f$, and let $T^\pm$ denote the Green/dynamical $(1,1)$-currents associated with $f$ and $f^{-1}$, with supports $J^\pm$, and let $J=J^+\cap J^-$. Let $J^*$ denote the closure of $\mathcal{S}$, and let $K^\pm$ denote the forward/backward filled-in sets. For each saddle $p\in\mathcal{S}$, write $E^u_p$ for the unstable direction at $p$ and $W^u_\varepsilon(p)$ for the local unstable manifold of radius $\varepsilon$.

Consider the following three conditions on $f$:

(1) Uniform unstable expansion: there exists $\kappa>1$ such that for every $p\in\mathcal{S}$ and every $v\in E^u_p$, $\|Df_p(v)\|\ge \kappa\|v\|$ in suitably chosen adapted metrics along the orbit of $p$.

(2) Proper, locally bounded area: there exist $\varepsilon>0$ and $A<\infty$ such that for every $p\in\mathcal{S}$, $W^u_\varepsilon(p)$ is closed in the ball $B(p,\varepsilon)$ and has area at most $A$.

(3$'$) The family of normalized unstable uniformizations $\hat\xi_p:\mathbb{C}\to X$, $p\in\mathcal{S}$, forms a normal family of entire mappings.

Call $f$ quasi-expanding if (1), (2), (3$'$) hold, and quasi-hyperbolic if both $f$ and $f^{-1}$ are quasi-expanding.

Questions:
(a) For such $f$, is Condition (3$'$) equivalent to the conjunction of (1) and (2)?
(b) If $f$ is quasi-hyperbolic, does the interior of $K^+$ consist of finitely many basins of attracting periodic orbits?
(c) If $f$ is quasi-hyperbolic, does $J = J^*$?
(d) If $f$ is quasi-hyperbolic, does $f$ have no wandering Fatou component?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a list of open problems on Hénon maps (2023/2024). The corresponding analogues for Hénon maps are known to be open in general; one of the related questions (no wandering Fatou components in the quasi-hyperbolic Hénon setting) has known counterexamples in degree 6 (Berger–Biebler), but these maps are not quasi-hyperbolic, so the quasi-hyperbolic version remains open. No published resolution for compact Kähler surface automorphisms was found.

status_evidence.title: Hénon Maps: A List of Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Questions 20, 21, 22 ... answers are 'yes' in the uniformly hyperbolic case, and the question is whether these properties remain true in the quasi-hyperbolic case.
status_evidence.claim: The questions are listed as open in the quasi-hyperbolic setting.
